claim: NRTA rules effective 1 September 2026 define microdramas as episodes shorter than 20 minutes with continuous story and characters; AI and multiple distribution devices are covered.
uncertainty: Statutory definition at cutoff; not a backcast classification of every historical publisher series.

claim: The report treats viewer expenditure and external advertising as final-demand measures and production, licensing, distribution and acquisition transfers as distinct chain flows.
uncertainty: Author accounting framework; proprietary published aggregate methodologies cannot be reconstructed.

claim: Top-ups, consumed virtual currency, recognized revenue and cash collection are different measures.
uncertainty: Company accounting/audit examples; principal-agent revenue policy depends on actual contract.

claim: PKU reports domestic market estimates RMB37.39bn 2023, 50.4bn 2024, about 100bn 2025; possible 200bn 2026 is a forecast.

claim: COL 2024 annual report cites 50.5bn 2024 estimate and 63.43bn 2025 forecast; Beijing June 2026 release calls national 2025 total 100bn output value and Beijing 58.57bn.

claim: Association white paper forecasts free viewing at 66.3% of full-year 2025 market.

claim: CNNIC estimates 662m/59.7% at December 2024 and 664m/59.0% at December 2025; implied count growth about 0.3%.
uncertainty: Survey estimates for mainland 6+ internet users; general proportion sampling errors are not a significance test for this category difference.

claim: CSM January 2026 adult survey reports 70.2% watching by end-2025, 84.2% future willingness to pay, and 71.8% having watched paid dramas in prior year.
uncertainty: Adult/sample boundary differs; willingness and watching paid content are not verified current paying conversion.

claim: QuestMobile February 2026 app MAU335m, WeChat mini-program427m and deduplicated union718m use different channel selection rules.
uncertainty: Apps selected at current MAU>100k and looked back; mini-programs independently selected each year MAU>1m; chart p6 visually confirmed.

claim: The February channel counts imply about 44m overlap; May three-channel sum exceeds 851m union by 73m memberships.

claim: May2026 apps402m, WeChat mini-program508m, Douyin mini-program14m comprise the851m application union;472m related-content reach is separately defined.

claim: September microdrama app MAU487m and Hongguo429.69m imply88.2% category penetration;380m co-use main Douyin,88.5% of Hongguo.

claim: January2025–May2026 monthly app hours13.0→26.9 and use occasions62.0→125.6 imply+106.9% hours,+102.6% occasions,and+2.1% minutes per occasion.

claim: Douyin documents organic, paid, and return traffic routes including feed, sidebar, search and subscriptions plus attributed ad yield information.
uncertainty: Documented capabilities, not measured favorable acquisition economics.

claim: Growth can be decomposed into active viewers, paying conversion/spend or repeat viewing, eligible ad inventory, fill and price.

claim: Association reports>140k vertical launches Jan–Aug2025 including repeats/re-edits, forecasts about40k independently completed annual productions, ordinary budgets400k–700k.

claim: Kuaishou reports an increase of more than 500% in drama supply from January to June 2026 and more than 100% year-on-year growth in Q2 microdrama online marketing expenditure.

claim: September HongguoMAU+81.8%,Hema−40.3%,Xingya−76.8%;Xifan8.34m+123.9% but belowMay11.018m.

claim: CSM reports>35% criticism of repetitive/unrealistic/unoriginal plots and11.8% preference for a fixed studio/account.

claim: WeChat mini-program users aged51+ comprise31.2% versus13.9% of app users inQMFebruary sample.

claim: PKU describes commissioned work, rights partnerships, finished-title submissions and reported seven-day exclusive opening windows.

claim: Hongguo announced planned content-budget growth>40% and greater sharing transparency;Douyin announcedRMB500m live-action support inApril.

claim: October reporting describes planned coin removal for newusers1Nov andallusersbyDecend, existing balance arrangements, and denial ofRMB40bn annualized revenue rumor.

claim: WeChat Lüpao Pao free service uses ads,social/regional recommendations and small-window viewing;Tencent agreement counterparty and third-party content suppliers.

claim: Same titles appear onHongguo andLüpao Pao;SeptemberLüpao PaoMAU156.35m precedesOctoberrecent-launch reporting.
uncertainty: Catalog overlap established, share of nonexclusive rights and exact launch/renaming chronology unresolved.

claim: May 2026 Douyin mini-program MAU fell 83.3% year on year while standalone apps and WeChat mini-programs grew.
uncertainty: Channel observations do not identify causal substitution to specific services.

claim: September Xifan MAU was 8.34 million; 6.32 million also used the main Kuaishou app.
uncertainty: Affiliation and overlap do not identify traffic transfer prices or guarantee equivalent app adoption.

claim: Tencent’s March 2026 policy provides an extra 15% on the pure-sharing settlement portion above RMB1 million and conditional longer sharing periods and series incentives.
uncertainty: Policy concerns exclusive horizontal long, mid and short formats; contractual box office is not raw consumer top-ups.

claim: QuestMobile’s policy compilation describes iQIYI platform-revenue-based sharing and Youku new-member and effective-play incentives.
uncertainty: Secondary compilation, not universal executed agreements or directly comparable sharing percentages.

claim: CSM paid-option preferences include membership and ad removal alongside interest in ad-supported or sharing-based free access.
uncertainty: Preferences do not identify price elasticity or realized hybrid profits.

claim: Douyin creator-promotion commissions of 1–29% and automatic initiation periods of up to 0–3 days differ from transaction settlement at T+7.
uncertainty: Different recipients and processes; neither number is a universal platform take rate.

claim: COL group revenue in 2023/2024/2025 was RMB1,408.9/1,159.1/1,656.6 million; parent profit 89.4/−242.9/−671.0 million; operating cash flow −10.1/−52.5/−203.7 million.

claim: CMS ceased consolidation from May2023: ownership49.16%, voting rights47.81%, three of seven board nominations; reported non-recurring profit effect55.9237m.

claim: iReader 2025 derivatives revenue1,854.9m and gross margin68%; group selling expense2,078.6m, promotion1,985.6m, gross profit less selling expense162.2m.

claim: iReader H1 2026 derivatives revenue1,185.1m, up41.45%; operating cash−116.5m versus nine-month52.7m implies Q3 inflow169.3m; revenue growth12.73% for nine months and5.96% for Q3.
uncertainty: Quarter cash flow is derived from cumulative group figures; not isolated domestic-drama economics.

claim: COL reports Yipin Buyi first-season plays above3bn and sequels; October reporting cites one March title with sharing above10m and200+ titles with monthly sharing above1m.
uncertainty: Selected corporate/news hits; plays are not unique users, settlement is not profit, and the complete slate denominator is unknown.

claim: Paid scenario:1m starts,4% conversion,RMB75 purchases,5% refunds,10% channel then10% rights,CAC1.20,budget600k yield508.5k project surplus.
uncertainty: All commercial inputs assumed; waterfall bases and excluded costs explicit.

claim: At2.5% paid conversion the producer loses357,187.50 after media-first recovery; break-even conversion is3.12%.
uncertainty: Loss allocation follows the assumed priority; more severe failure can also impair media recovery.

claim: A1m production budget cuts paid-case surplus to108.5k; a12% refund rate cuts it to338.4k with other base inputs fixed.
uncertainty: One-variable sensitivities, not observed industry ranges.

claim: Free scenario:1m viewers ×14 active days ×(4+8×60%) ad opportunities ×80% fill ×RMB20/1,000 generates1,971,200 advertiser expenditure.
uncertainty: Assumed later-block reach is distinct from actual observed retention, full-series completion and ad completion.

claim: Free case:20% network deduction,35% content share,CAC0.70,100k operating cost and600k production cost yield platform225,024,producer−48,064,joint176,960.
uncertainty: Explicit assumptions; a platform can earn a positive contribution while its content supplier loses money.

claim: Free-case platform break-even10.93 days and producer15.22 days; content share45% gives producer109,632/platform67,328 without changing joint surplus.
uncertainty: Comparative statics; changing sharing alone creates no additional revenue.

claim: Removing60k of assumed rewards is offset by losing0.82 active days, or5.85% of the14-day base.
uncertainty: Sensitivity threshold, not a prediction of Hongguo’s reward withdrawal.

claim: Hybrid example:50k RMB7 passes net299,250 after refunds/fees; subtracting78,848 displaced average advertising yields incremental publisher receipts220,402; double-ad-value buyers yield141,554.
uncertainty: Before extra service and content-sharing costs; not platform net profit or an optimal price estimate.

claim: Production, acquisition payment, revenue recognition and collection may occur at different times; T+7 is one transaction step.
uncertainty: Cash-cycle inference; no industry-wide recovery duration is asserted.

claim: Earlier NRTA June2024 implementation differs from February2025 webpage date; live-action thresholds adjusted January2026, AI thresholds July2026, and comprehensive measures effective September2026.
uncertainty: Effective dates, signature dates and webpage dates are kept separate.

claim: CategoryI covers special subjects or live-action investment>=3m/AI>=800k; II ordinary live1m–<3m/AI300k–<800k; III lower budgets subject to platform review.
uncertainty: Thresholds come from the local official implementation explanation, not a claimed copy of the original national threshold circular.

claim: CategoryI decision period20 days from acceptance including10 days expert review; changes require resubmission; non-exclusiveIII uses each outlet’s number and rebroadcast review; AI episodes require labels.
uncertainty: The period is not an end-to-end script-to-release guarantee.

claim: The2026 quality plan targets1,000 works by year-end with funding, creative and distribution support plus application/delivery requirements.
uncertainty: Target and policy resources, not an achieved count or confirmed disbursement.

claim: November6 announcement covers a November1–December-end campaign;75,000 removals and1,500+ accounts addressed refer to earlier2026 actions.
uncertainty: Does not present earlier figures as results of the new campaign; profit impacts are not quantified.

claim: Consumer regulation requires clear pricing, renewal notice, limits on unfair terms, and prepaid-service contract/refund obligations.
uncertainty: Retained official text supplies no universal five-day renewal notice period.

claim: Douyin rules require full prices, stable tokens, affirmative consent, quarter-length maximum membership,10h×7days support,15-minute responses and48-hour complaint handling.
uncertainty: Specific to the frozen platform rule, not universal contracts for the whole industry.

claim: Douyin mandates full refunds for minors’ virtual-goods purchases regardless of fulfillment; Civil Code capacity depends on age, transaction and guardian consent or ratification.
uncertainty: Platform commercial rules do not establish that all minors’ transactions are automatically void nationally.

claim: Court case introduction describes a renamed unauthorized drama, paid traffic routing and RMB46,000 covering damages and reasonable enforcement expenses.
uncertainty: Case introduction, not the full judgment; amount includes damages and expenses and is not a general tariff.

claim: Repeat access, rights and cash recovery are central competitive assets, but no universal platform or monetization-model winner is established.
uncertainty: Author synthesis; unmatched platform cohorts do not identify causal advantages.

claim: Platforms should compare reward savings with lost cohort advertising value and maintain viable content supply.
uncertainty: Conditional recommendation; retention, yield and supplier response must be observed.

claim: Producer choices between guarantees and contingent sharing depend on financing, rights, windows and recovery priority.
uncertainty: Recommendation requires actual contracts, full portfolio costs and failure rates.

claim: Investors should reconcile controlled entities, geography, acquisition costs and cash recovery before valuing market growth.
uncertainty: Recommendation would change with representative positive recovery after promotion, failures, obligations and refunds.

claim: CP23 contains only an access failure; CP10/CP20 are retained web outputs; MDX002 duplicates CP27 and CP15/CP17 are the same underlying research.
